page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-highmem-2 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance based on the x86_64 architecture. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to a single physical AMD EPYC 7B13 core with 2 threads. The hardware configuration includes 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. The processor is equipped with 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It supports hardware-assisted features such as Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX), AES and VAES cryptography, and SHA_NI. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and it is provisioned with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data reveals a stark contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. The instance demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance in stress-ng tests, placing in the top 25%. However, its multi-core CPU performance and overall PassMark CPU score fall into the bottom 25%, reflecting the physical limitations of its single-core, dual-thread design. Memory subsystem benchmarks show weak to poor performance, with read-only small block cached bandwidth in the bottom 10% (138.13 GB/sec) and large block uncached write bandwidth at 24.29 GB/sec. Similarly, database operations and software compilation benchmarks score in the bottom 10%, indicating that the instance is not suited for heavy concurrent write operations or intensive parallel builds.

In terms of qualitative cost efficiency, the c2d-highmem-2 offers a high memory footprint relative to its low vCPU count, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not require high parallel processing power. Single-threaded tasks, such as gzip compression and bzip3 decompression, perform at average levels. Additionally, small-scale LLM text generation (135M model) achieves an average speed of 79.09 tokens/sec, though prompt processing remains slow. This instance is best suited for lightweight memory-intensive applications, basic text processing, single-threaded scripting, and low-throughput web serving.
